seoDescription: Learn the complete workflow for building and deploying Ionic Capacitor applications for both Android and iOS. This guide covers creating a new Ionic Angular project, configuring your app's unique ID, and adding native platforms. Follow step-by-step instructions to run your app on an Android emulator and iOS simulator, sync changes effectively, and open projects in Android Studio and Xcode. Master the process of generating both a debug APK and a signed release APK for distribution on Android devices.

chapters.title: Introduction to Ionic Capacitor Builds
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the video's topic of building an APK with Ionic Capacitor and running it on Android and iOS devices and emulators.

chapters.title: Creating a New Ionic Angular Project
chapters.description: This chapter walks through the process of creating a new blank Ionic Angular project using the Ionic CLI.

chapters.title: Serving the App in a Browser
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to run the newly created Ionic application in a local browser using the 'ionic serve' command.

chapters.title: Configuring App ID and Name
chapters.description: This chapter explains how to configure the application's unique ID and name in the capacitor.config.ts file and run 'ionic build'.

chapters.title: Adding Native Android & iOS Platforms
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to add the native project folders for Android and iOS using the 'ionic capacitor add' command.

chapters.title: Running the App on an Android Emulator
chapters.description: This chapter covers syncing code changes and using 'ionic cap open android' to run the application on an Android emulator via Android Studio.

chapters.title: Generating a Debug & Signed APK
chapters.description: This chapter provides a detailed walkthrough of generating both a simple debug APK and a signed release APK using Android Studio.

chapters.title: Running the App on an iOS Simulator
chapters.description: This chapter details opening the project in Xcode, configuring a signing team, and running the application on an iOS simulator.

chapters.title: Conclusion & Final Recommendations
chapters.description: This chapter summarizes how to launch the app on simulators, build an APK, and provides final recommendations and a channel outro.

summary:
## Getting Started

*   **Create Project**: Use `ionic start <project-name> blank --type=angular` to initialize a new Ionic Angular application.
*   **Serve Locally**: Run `ionic serve` to test your application in a web browser before building for native platforms.

## App Configuration

*   Before building, edit the `capacitor.config.ts` file to configure your app's identity.
*   **appId**: This must be a unique identifier, conventionally in reverse domain name notation (e.g., `com.yourdomain.appname`).
*   **appName**: The user-facing name of your application.
*   **Run Production Build**: Execute `ionic build`. This command creates the `www` folder, which contains the compiled web assets necessary for the native builds.

## Adding Native Platforms

*   Use the Ionic CLI to add native project folders:
    *   `ionic cap add android`
    *   `ionic cap add ios`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Whenever you make changes to your web code (HTML, TS, CSS), you must sync them to the native projects. Use the command `ionic cap sync` to copy your web assets and update the native configurations.

## Android Workflow

1.  **Open in Android Studio**: Use the command `ionic cap open android`.
2.  **Run on Emulator**: In Android Studio, select a virtual device from the dropdown menu and click the 'Run' button (▶️).
3.  **Generate an APK**:
    *   **Debug APK**: For testing, go to `Build > Build Bundle(s) / APK(s) > Build APK(s)`. The resulting `app-debug.apk` can be found in `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/`.
    *   **Signed Release APK**: For distribution, go to `Build > Generate Signed Bundle / APK`. You will need to create a **keystore** with a password and key alias.

> [!TIP]
> For publishing on the Google Play Store, it's highly recommended to generate an **Android App Bundle (.aab)** instead of an APK, as it allows for optimized delivery.

## iOS Workflow

1.  **Prerequisites**: You must have a Mac with **Xcode** installed.
2.  **Open in Xcode**: Use the command `ionic cap open ios`.
3.  **Configure Signing**: In your project's target settings under the **Signing & Capabilities** tab, you must select a **Team**. A free personal team created with your Apple ID is sufficient for development and testing on your own devices.
4.  **Run on Simulator**: In Xcode, select an iOS simulator (e.g., iPhone 14 Pro) from the device list and click the 'Run' button (▶️).
5.  **Run on Physical Device**: Connect your iPhone via USB, select it from the device list in Xcode, and click 'Run'.
